title: A bus that survives: failures and leaks
tasks: ResilientBus(EventBus): override _deliver so a handler's exception is caught and recorded in a bounded errors deque
Catch Exception only, so interrupts and timeouts still stop the program
subscribe_weak(name, method): subscribe through a forwarding closure that holds only a weak reference
Replace the hub's bus, reconnect the lights, and add bus_errors() for the scene
explanation: Because every call goes through _deliver, one overridden method adds isolation to the whole bus. Failures become data (event, sequence, handler, message) in a bounded box instead of exceptions thrown at the publisher. A weak subscription stores only a WeakMethod; its forwarding closure unsubscribes itself the first time it finds the owner gone, so forgotten listeners clean up after themselves.

hints.title: Isolating failures
hints.content: def _deliver(self, subscription, event): try: subscription.handler(event) except Exception as err: self.errors.append({"event": event.name, "seq": event.seq, "handler": getattr(subscription.handler, "__qualname__", repr(subscription.handler)), "error": f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"}); return False. After the try/except, return True. In __init__ call super().__init__(history_size) and create self.errors = deque(maxlen=50).

hints.title: Weak subscriptions
hints.content: reference = weakref.WeakMethod(method) if inspect.ismethod(method) else weakref.ref(method). Define def forward(event): target = reference(); if target is None: unsubscribe() else: target(event). Then unsubscribe = self.subscribe(name, forward) and return unsubscribe. forward can use unsubscribe because it is only called after the assignment.

hints.title: Swapping the bus
hints.content: bus = ResilientBus() then stop_following = connect_lights(bus), because the old bus's subscriptions do not move. bus_errors() is list(bus.errors). world_event and event_log keep working unchanged because they look up the global name bus each time they run.

checks.prompt: Why should `_deliver` catch `Exception` rather than use a bare `except:`?

options: A bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and timeouts, so the program could not be stopped
Exception catches more error types than a bare except
Python does not allow a bare except inside a method

checks.explanation: Those signals derive from `BaseException`, not `Exception`. They exist so you can interrupt a program; a handler wrapper should isolate ordinary bugs, not make the whole process unkillable.

checks.prompt: A dashboard object subscribes `self.refresh` to the bus in `__init__`, and later the program drops every reference to the dashboard. With a normal (strong) subscription, what happens?

options: The dashboard is freed and stops receiving events
The bus's reference to the bound method keeps the dashboard alive and it keeps receiving events
Python raises an error when the last reference is dropped

checks.explanation: A bound method holds its instance, and the bus holds the bound method, so the instance can never be collected. Fix it with an explicit `close()` that calls unsubscribe, or a weak subscription.

checks.prompt: Why is `weakref.ref(panel.on_event)` almost useless for a weak subscription?

options: Weak references only work on classes
`panel.on_event` creates a fresh bound-method object each time, and nothing else holds it, so it is freed immediately
weakref cannot refer to methods at all
It works fine; WeakMethod is only a shortcut

checks.explanation: Each evaluation of `panel.on_event` builds a temporary bound-method object. Using `weakref.WeakMethod` stores weak references to the instance and function separately and rebuilds the method when asked.
